items.title: `process::scan()` answers "" on EVERY call on the JS backend since v0.33.0: the `__scan` helper calls `require("fs")` inside the emitted ES module (`.mjs` since B86b, e5a809c0), and its own `catch` swallows the `ReferenceError` - `printf 'a\nb\n' \| vilan run p.vl` prints three empty lines
items.body: `transformer.rs::helper_source("__scan")` fills its line array with `require("fs").readFileSync(0, "utf-8").split("\n")` in a `try`, falling back to `[]` on any error; an `.mjs` has no `require`, so the fallback always runs. Unnoticed because nothing calls `scan()` (zero uses in the tree, the corpus, kolt and the website; the corpus runs programs with stdin `Stdio::null()`). A173 S1 replaces the helper wholesale (an incremental awaiting reader); if S1 slips, the one-line fix is `process.getBuiltinModule("node:fs").readFileSync(0, "utf-8")` (synchronous, valid in an ES module on node >= 22.3), plus a pin that pipes two lines through `vilan run`. `fix`.

items.kind: miscompile (both backends; the context threading pass vs the for-in desugar)
items.status: FIXED - filed and closed on arrival, Order 54 (solver-54, merge 68666705); the filing lane's find was fixed by that lane's merge
items.title: A `for x in subject` whose `next` reads a context - any std IO wait (`time::sleep`, through `ambient_signal()`), or `task::ambient_signal()` itself in a SYNC `impl .. with Iterator<i32>` - is emitted without the threaded context argument: check-clean, JS crashes `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')`, native fails cargo (E0061, 'a BACKEND defect')
items.body: The same `next` called directly (`direct.next()`) gets its context argument (`next($g, $a)`); the loop's implicit call is emitted `next($g)` on JS and `next_N(&mut iterator)` natively. The for-in's desugared `next` call is outside the context threading pass's call-site walk (a binder the loop lowering mints, not a call the source wrote). Rec: thread the context at the loop's `next` exactly as at a written call, on both backends; pins: the sync context-reading `Iterator`, the async inherent `next(self)` over a `Shared` cursor, both printing the same on JS and native. Unblocks `for key in keys` for A173 S2 (with F-3). Estate: no program in kolt/the website/the corpus iterates such a subject (they would crash). `miscompile`.

items.status: FIXED - filed and closed on arrival, Order 54 (native-54, merge a6a1d983); the filing lane's find was fixed by that lane's merge
items.title: Native: a `for x in subject` over a type whose INHERENT `next(self): Option<T>` awaits (the checker accepts it - spec §3.5's iteration protocol) is emitted as `while let Some(x) = next_N(&mut iterator)` with no `.await`; cargo refuses (E0308 'expected future, found Option'). JS awaits it (and only fails on B644's context argument)
items.body: The emitter's for-in lowering does not ask whether the subject's `next` is async. Rec: await it as the JS lowering does (and take the receiver by the shape `next` declares - `&mut iterator` for a by-value `self` is the other half of the same rustc error list); pin with B644's async probe once both land. The trait form (`Iterator::next(&mut self)`) stays refused for async by the `&mut`-across-suspension rule - this is only the inherent by-value form.

items.title: The native backend implements `process::env` but refuses `scan` (intrinsic `Scan`), `args` (intrinsic `Args`), `exit` and `cwd` (host bindings `process.exit` / `process.cwd`) with F1's S1b refusal - four of std::process's five functions
items.body: Each is a few lines of Rust std in vilan-rt (`std::env::args().skip(1)`, `std::process::exit` after flushing stdout, `std::env::current_dir`), no dependency. Rec: land them with A173 S1 so the S1 pins (a prompt that exits non-zero on bad input) and every CLI example build both ways; the differential's refusal census drops four rows.

items.status: OPEN - filed 2026-10-16 (papers-54's find, Order 54); NARROWED by A173 S1's prompt(text) (std-54, 15d98d85): the general io::write stays, closed with S2
items.title: std has no way to write to stdout WITHOUT a newline: `io::print` is `console.log` (JS) / `println!` (native) and there is no other stdout door, so an interactive prompt (`name? ` with the cursor after it), a progress line or any terminal redraw cannot be written
items.body:
A173's Q2 recommends `process::prompt(text)` for the prompt case in S1 (written unterminated and FLUSHED - Rust's stdout is a LineWriter); the general `io::write(text)` (stdout, no newline, flushed) is recommended for A173 S2, where every key-driven redraw needs it. Both backends: `process.stdout.write` / `print!` + `flush`.

Order 54 note: A173 S1's `process::prompt(text): Option<str>` (std-54, 15d98d85; a private `__stdout_write`) writes an unterminated, flushed line before it reads, which answers the prompt half. What stays open is the GENERAL no-newline stdout (`io::write(text)`), which S2's key loop and any redraw need; it closes with S2 (the owner's rec in std-54's hand-back: yes).

items.title: Under `VILAN_STD_PREFIX=on` the phase census prints `prefix-world 0 prefix-refusal -` for a program that silently does not take the prefix (8 corpus programs: every one that builds a macro world - `crypto`, `db`, `file`, `watch`, `interpolated-multiline-string`, `macro-block`, `macro-derive`, `macro-invoke`): the column says neither served nor why
items.body: The prefix is not attempted when reuse is not allowed (a macro world makes the base world uncacheable), and no refusal reason is noted, so a census over the estate reads those programs as unexplained. Rec: `note_prefix_refusal("uncacheable")` (or the reuse gate's own reason) where `std_prefix_wanted` is false only because reuse is off, so P6a's census and P6b's default can count every program by name. XS; `tooling`.
